note: PiCode's own pi, pinned to an exact version so a freshly built editor is born working. `dev/pi-runtime.sh` installs it during the build and the connector looks for it there — nobody has to install or configure it. **1.0.4 → 1.1.0, a normal step**: the 1.1.0 changelog has no breaking change and nothing that reaches this product. PiCode passes none of pi's `--tools`/`-t`, `--exclude-tools` or `--no-mcp` (the only `--no-mcp` in the tree belongs to PiCode's durable daemon, not to pi), so the new `+name`/`-name` tool entries change nothing here, and Claude Haiku 5.5 plus the new classifier models (GPT-6 Luna, the llama.cpp decision models) arrive through pi's own catalogue, which the model picker already reads — nothing to declare. What does reach the owner is a set of fixes: Anthropic browser login falling back to a free loopback port when 53692 is reserved (Hyper-V/WSL on Windows), MCP OAuth sign-ins cancellable at every step with a 15 s per-request timeout and no 15 s wait at shutdown, `/mcp` opening live while servers connect, `server_busy` and Mistral `finish_reason: "error"` responses retried instead of ending the turn, input estimated at 3.5 chars/token to reduce context-limit failures, session costs no longer undercounting long prompts on prompt-length pricing tiers, and a model's `headers` in `models.json` now overriding Codex `originator`/`User-Agent`. Verified against 1.1.0 on 2026-10-08 before pinning: the connector's 7 SDK entries resolve, `dist/cli.js` and `dist/extensions/index.js` (4 built-ins) are present, and pi's own MCP validator accepts all 12 writers PiCode emits while still rejecting the two legacy spellings (`dev/check-mcp-entries.mjs`).
